claims.invariant: Apache Airflow is the only managed lifecycle scheduler and every managed run is bound to a durable Factory Cell epoch.
claims.environment: GitHub-hosted Ubuntu with upstream Airflow plus authenticated live-gate harness

claims.invariant: Every managed GitHub write carries the current Cell epoch, policy, operation identity and durable observation/replay contract.
claims.environment: backend-owned GitHub credentials; coding sandboxes receive no publication secret

claims.invariant: Ambiguous effects remain in_doubt until observation proves committed or definitely absent; stale epochs cannot repair or replay them.
claims.environment: durable SQLite journal with restart/reconciliation tests

claims.invariant: Plan.work executes only inside the Airflow-owned build stage, honors dependencies and conflicts, and fans in deterministically.
claims.runtime_entry: swfactory.work_stage.build_and_test (the Airflow build task dags/blueprints.py selects) -> bounded Plan.work execution
claims.environment: supported serial fallback on the governed build workspace

claims.invariant: Parallel candidates need immutable parent identity, isolated workspaces, bounded leases and deterministic conflict-aware fan-in.
claims.environment: provider-specific; not part of the supported promotion contract
claims.test: tests/test_work_executor.py (parallel fan-out, conflict, crash and cancellation scenarios)
claims.follow_up: Qualify one real provider with isolated candidate workspaces and retained lineage before changing support to validated.

claims.invariant: The keyless scripted path contains no model or publishing credential and produces a verified local delivery.
claims.test: ci:test required job (its e2e demo step) plus tests/test_stages_scripted.py

claims.invariant: OS confinement and protected-write policy are verified independently of publication authority.
claims.test: ci:srt-smoke plus the SrtSandbox argv contracts in tests/test_sandbox_argv.py
claims.follow_up: Promote only after the hosted smoke is stable enough to join a required protected-branch context.

claims.invariant: Container execution is isolated from publication authority and passes the scripted delivery contract.
claims.follow_up: Keep advisory until failure rate and cleanup semantics satisfy the supported sandbox SLO.

claims.invariant: Child factories are isolated, budgeted and cannot self-promote into the parent production authority.
claims.runtime_entry: generation manifests and parent-owned promotion path
claims.follow_up: Require a parent-approved adoption/refusal/rollback experiment with no parent production credentials before operational support.

claims.invariant: Agent MicroVMs hold no publication authority: the GitHub credential exists only in the trusted orchestrator, the agent VM never receives an SCM token, and it reaches the network only through the deny-by-default swfactory gateway profile. The target's protected-path list is agent-enforced here (permissions.deny plus the PreToolUse hook), not kernel-enforced: IsloSandbox has no set_protected and stages applies the per-stage tightening only when the backend exposes one.
claims.runtime_entry: swfactory.sandbox.IsloSandbox (islo use / cp / rm control plane)
claims.environment: islo MicroVMs: one trusted orchestrator VM plus one untrusted agent VM per job; requires ISLO_API_KEY and the swfactory gateway profile described in docs/islo.md
claims.test: ci:evals-islo in .github/workflows/evals.yml (a real claude run inside a MicroVM) plus the hermetic argv contracts in tests/test_sandbox_argv.py
evidence: CI job ci:evals-islo (workflow evals.yml; self-skips when the ISLO_API_KEY secret is unset, so a green result does not prove a MicroVM ran)
claims.follow_up: Promote only once evals-islo runs unconditionally on main-bound candidates, joins the candidate-readiness required set, and lands its receipt in the SHA-bound readiness manifest. The credential-separation invariant additionally needs a negative test proving an agent VM cannot obtain GH_TOKEN, and kernel-level protected-path enforcement needs an IsloSandbox.set_protected.

claims.invariant: A self-hosted run cannot weaken its own governing policy: the factory's own factory.toml, required CI contexts, blueprints, DAGs, capability inventory and confinement modules are refused as agent-writable paths, and a self-produced change reaches main only through a human release gate on a branch the agent held no credential to push.
claims.runtime_entry: swfactory run --blueprint selfhost (target dir is the repo root), executing swfactory.stages against the factory's own tree
claims.environment: islo MicroVM agent cells in production and local Docker sandboxes on a developer box; in both the orchestrator holds the only GitHub credential
claims.test: tests/test_selfhost.py (contract parses, every protected entry survives literal-prefix reduction, confinement modules are refused for build and fix, both gates are non-auto, one line serves both backends)
evidence: advisory check ci:control-plane-gate (base-revision protected list vs the PR diff; not required on main)
claims.follow_up: No end-to-end evidence exists yet: no self-hosted run has produced a merged pull request on either backend. Before any change of state, archive one full self-hosted run per backend (islo and docker) whose PR a human merged, and settle whether `islo use --init minimal` executes the repo-root islo.yaml setup script that installs uv.

claims.invariant: SmolVM execution keeps host authority outside the guest, fences interrupted operations, and retains unconfirmed cleanup debt.
claims.environment: Dedicated Linux/KVM host with an operator-owned SmolVM Unix socket; live qualification required
claims.follow_up: Qualify the pinned runtime with real VM checks, close the observation/auto-start race, and add cancellation-aware lineage before enabling forks.
